title: Maximum Sum With Even/Prime Rules
statement:
You are given a list `a` of `n` positive integers and a number `N`. Choose **exactly `N` elements** of the list, i.e. choose `N` positions, so that the sum of the chosen elements is as large as possible. The chosen elements are reported in their original order. The choice must obey two rules:

- **Even rule:** if you choose an even element whose value is **not** `2`, you must also choose the element immediately after it in the list. (So such an element cannot be chosen if it is the last element of the list.)
- **Prime rule:** if you choose an element whose value is prime (this includes `2`; `1` is not prime), you must **not** choose the element immediately after it.

Every chosen element counts toward `N`, including elements you were forced to take by the even rule. Rules apply to every chosen element, so a forced element can itself force or forbid the next one.

If several choices give the same maximum sum, print the one whose list of chosen positions is **lexicographically smallest** (compare the increasing position lists element by element). If no valid choice of exactly `N` elements exists, print `-1`.

Print the values of the chosen elements in original order.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `N`.
The second line contains `n` integers: the list `a`.
outputFormat: Print the `N` chosen values in their original order, separated by single spaces, or print `-1` if no valid choice exists.

examples.explanation: Choosing 4 forces 6, and 6 forces 9, so these three are taken together for a sum of 19. The element 8 is even and last, so it can never be chosen. The other valid choice, 1, 6, 9, only reaches 16.
Every element is prime, so no two neighbouring elements can both be chosen. The best valid choice takes the first and the last: 3 and 7.
All three elements would have to be chosen, but 3 is prime and forbids 5. No valid choice exists.

hints: Try scanning the list left to right with a state: how many elements you have chosen so far, and whether the previous element was chosen.

Whether the current element is forced or forbidden depends only on the value of the previous element, and only if the previous one was chosen. So the state (position, count, previous chosen or not) is enough.

Compute the best sum from the back (suffix DP), then rebuild the answer from the front: at each position, take the element whenever doing so still reaches the optimal sum. This gives the lexicographically smallest positions on ties.
